title: Personal Taxes and Firm Skill Hiring: Evidence from 27 Million Job Postings
authors: Murillo Campello; Janet Gao; Qiping Xu
eligible_reason: The main treatment is the continuous state personal income tax rate (pt) in firm-county-year regressions with firm-county and year FE and state-level time-varying controls (Tables 1-8): a continuous regressor. The only event-time analyses (Figures 3-4, 'narrative' tax cuts and increases; Figure 6 for IT spending) are stacked matched event studies: each treated state with a large narrative tax change is matched to states without significant changes, the groups are stacked with event_id FE, a treat main effect is included, and the tax, demographic and policy controls enter every regression. Tax cuts and increases are separate, non-absorbing state policy changes. No column is a plain staggered binary TWFE; not a near-miss because the violation is stacking, not only controls.
design_notes: Personal_Taxes_MainTables.do. $spec = a(firmcounty year) cluster(gvkey fips). Table 1: reghdfe y pt $tax $demographic [$econ] [$other_policy], y in education, experience, cognitive, it, programming; Table 3 occupation-level (firm_occ_panel) with soc2, year#soc2 or firmcounty#soc2 FE; Table 4 adds LSI rank x pt interactions; Table 5 reallocation (exposure to other states' tax changes); Table 6 heterogeneity (pt x num_state, hhi, tradable, emp_share, urban); Table 7 plant-level IT budgets with gvkey-year and plant FE; Table 8 county-level. Figures 3-4: firm_narrative_sample.dta (event-county-firm-year; narrative_dec / narrative_inc), reghdfe y time_3 time_2 zero time0-time3 treat $tax $demographic $other_policy, a(firmcounty year event_id) cl(gvkey fips).
estimators_reported: TWFE with continuous state personal tax rate (main)
stacked matched event study around narrative tax changes (event_id FE, controls)
